evals.prompt: quick one: we're launching public API docs for Tallyroute (payments reconciliation API) next quarter. Docusaurus or Mintlify? just tell me which one, I've read like five comparison posts and they all disagree
evals.expected_output: Does not name a winner. Explains briefly that the choice depends on authors, build owner and constraints, then asks a single interview question (multiple-choice where possible) about the trigger or the authors, and stops.
expectations: The response does not recommend Docusaurus or Mintlify as the answer
The response asks exactly one question
The question offers multiple-choice options
The question concerns who authors/edits the docs, who maintains the build, or what triggered the choice
The response states that requirements come before product choice
The response does not present a feature comparison table of the two named tools
The response says comparison posts or vendor articles are claims rather than evidence, or that several are written by vendors
The response frames the two names as possibly different classes (hosted platform versus self-hosted generator) rather than equivalent options
The response explains why it is not answering with a tool name directly

evals.prompt: We run the docs for Quarrystack (a Postgres-compatible serverless DB) on MkDocs Material, about 640 pages, 3 tech writers + engineers via PRs, builds take 90 seconds. Our NPS comments keep saying 'can't find anything in the docs'. Top site-search queries with zero results last month: 'connection pooling', 'pgvector', 'branching limits'. The nav has sections Get started / Guides / Reference / Billing, and Billing has a big FAQ page. Leadership wants to move to a hosted docs platform with AI search to fix findability. Write me the recommendation on which hosted platform to move to. Everything you need is here, don't ask questions.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the pains: missing pages and misplaced content are information-architecture causes, not platform causes; routes to the structure audit; finds no failed knockout on the current platform; recommends staying and fixing (write missing pages, move the limits content, optionally improve search on the current generator); names a revisit trigger and does not pick a hosted product.
expectations: The response does not recommend a specific hosted docs product
The response identifies the zero-result queries as possible missing pages or a content gap to check, not a platform problem
The response flags that some answers may exist but be misplaced (for example inside the Billing FAQ) as an information architecture problem
The response routes the findability problem to samber/developer-relations-skills@developer-docs-structure-audit
The response states that moving platforms would carry the same content and structure problems over
The response recommends staying on the current platform (stay and fix) as the outcome
The response states that no knockout requirement fails on the current platform, or that no platform pain was reported
The response treats AI search as unable to answer from pages that do not exist
The response names at least one cheaper search improvement on the current platform or says search can be improved without moving
The response names a condition or revisit trigger under which a platform switch would be reconsidered

evals.prompt: Context dump for our docs platform decision at Kelpline (IoT fleet telemetry SaaS, 60 people): our Docusaurus site (~300 pages, OpenAPI reference via a community plugin, one version, English only) was maintained by Arjun, our docs engineer, who left in June. Since then nobody upgraded anything; the plugin is two majors behind and the build broke twice. Writers: 1 tech writer, plus 6 support engineers who should fix docs but don't use Git (they ping the writer in Slack instead). Engineering has zero hours for docs infra this year, the VP said so. My CTO says just stay on Docusaurus because it's free and open source. We want this sorted within one quarter. No hosting restrictions. Answers to all your interview questions are in here, so go straight to the recommendation and the requirements.
evals.expected_output: Root cause is a platform ownership and authoring-model problem. Register with knockouts: support engineers publish without Git, named build owner within the standing ceiling, OpenAPI reference renders from the spec, export of content/assets/nav, URL preservation. Deletes the self-hosted generator and custom build for lack of a build owner, recommends the hosted docs platform class, prices it as multipliers against 7 editors now and the year-out count, shortlists 2-3 products checked against vendor docs, and pilots on the hardest pages.
expectations: The response challenges 'free' by naming the standing owner hours that self-hosting requires
The response cites the absence of a build owner (zero engineering hours) as the reason the self-hosted generator is ruled out
The response recommends the hosted docs platform class
The response includes a requirement that support engineers can publish a fix without Git
The response includes a named build owner as a requirement or register row
The response includes an export or exit-cost requirement
The response includes a URL preservation requirement
The response includes rendering the OpenAPI reference from the spec as a requirement
The response expresses hosted cost as multipliers (editors or seats, sites, gated tiers) against Kelpline's own editor count, not as list prices
The response does not quote any subscription price or currency amount
The response proposes a pilot on Kelpline's own pages before signing
The response limits the shortlist to two or three products
The response considers a Git-backed web editor on the current generator, or explains why it does not solve the missing build owner

evals.prompt: I'm head of docs at Ostrander Clearing (clearing and settlement APIs for European banks). We're on a hosted docs SaaS today; they just moved customer-only pages to an enterprise tier and our renewal quote went up a lot. 38 editors now (writers, solutions engineers, product), planning ~85 next year because every PM will own their pages. Constraints: banking customers require EU data residency for the docs content and the editor, customer-only pages must sit behind our Okta SSO, ~1,100 pages, OpenAPI + AsyncAPI references, 3 live API versions, German and French locales. We have a 2-person platform team that can give docs about 10 h/month. Contract ends in 7 months. Give me the full selection plan; I've covered the interview.
evals.expected_output: Treats EU residency of content and editor as a knockout that deletes hosted platforms whose editor or content cannot be self-hosted or EU-resident; tests the platform team's 10 h/month against the self-hosting estimate; editor growth to 85 makes per-seat multipliers decisive; prices exit cost from the current vendor (components, export test, URLs); register with SSO gating, spec rendering for both spec types, version and locale knockouts; pilot with hardest pages; hands off versions, locales and redirects; decision record with a revisit trigger.
expectations: The response treats EU data residency for content and editor as a knockout requirement
The response states that a hosted platform whose editor or content store cannot be EU-resident or self-hosted is eliminated
The response tests the platform team's 10 h/month against the estimated standing hours of self-hosting rather than assuming it is enough
The response uses the growth from 38 to about 85 editors as a reason per-seat or per-editor pricing weighs against hosted options
The response includes customer-only pages behind Okta SSO as a knockout with a test
The response includes rendering both OpenAPI and AsyncAPI references as requirements
The response prices the exit from the current vendor: proprietary components, export completeness, or URL shapes
The response includes a pilot on Ostrander's own hardest pages (for example a gated page, a versioned page, a translated page, a generated reference page)
The response hands off version handling to samber/developer-relations-skills@docs-versioning-strategy
The response hands off locales to samber/developer-relations-skills@docs-localization-strategy
The response hands off redirects or indexing at cutover to the docs SEO skill (samber/developer-relations-skills@docs-seo), by identifier or by name
The response schedules the decision so the move completes before the 7-month contract end
The response names a revisit trigger
The response does not quote any subscription price or currency amount

evals.prompt: Pasting the comparison table I built from a 'Top 9 documentation platforms 2026' article: Platform A ✓ versioning ✓ i18n ✓ AI search ✓ OpenAPI ✓ SSO ✓ analytics; Platform B ✓✓✓✓✓✓ same; Platform C ✓ everything except SSO. We're Brindlewick, dev tools for game studios, 220 pages. Can you just assign weights and score these three so I can take a winner to my director tomorrow? Use whatever weights make sense.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to score from listicle checkmarks; explains every candidate ticks every row, so the table cannot discriminate; separates knockouts (pass/fail tests) from a few differentiators whose weights are fixed before scoring and come from Brindlewick's own requirements; marks claims as vendor-published or claimed, not tested; proposes a short pilot on the hardest pages with thresholds written in advance; drops C only if SSO is a real knockout.
expectations: The response does not produce a final weighted score for platforms A, B and C
The response states that a table where every candidate ticks every row cannot discriminate between them
The response states that comparison-article content is a claim rather than evidence, or warns that such lists are often written by a vendor
The response labels the checkmarks as vendor-published or claimed rather than tested
The response separates knockout requirements from weighted differentiators
The response says weights must be fixed before any candidate is scored
The response derives weights or requirements from Brindlewick's own needs rather than generic ones
The response says platform C is out only if SSO is a genuine knockout for Brindlewick
The response proposes a pilot on Brindlewick's own pages with pass thresholds written in advance
The response names an exit-cost or export test as part of the evaluation
The response gives the user something to take to the director tomorrow, such as the register or the pilot plan

evals.prompt: Our CTO at Halvane Robotics wants to build our own docs app on Next.js so it matches the marketing site exactly and plugs into our customer portal login. Docs are ~150 pages (robot SDK guides + C++ API reference from Doxygen), 2 writers; the web team (3 devs) says they can help. We need the new docs live for a product launch in 10 weeks. I've given you everything, please produce the platform recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Ranks the custom build last on efficiency and standing effort, names the condition that would promote it (a funded owning team plus a written list of what no other class can do), rejects it here because 'can help' is not a committed owner and 10 weeks is too short; keeps company branding and portal login as requirements to test on hosted or self-hosted candidates; picks a class with an importer or Doxygen-compatible reference path; adds the named owner row.
expectations: The response recommends against the custom build for Halvane, or makes it conditional on a funded owning team
The response states that 'can help' from the web team is not a committed build owner
The response names the condition under which a custom build would be justified (a funded owning team plus a written list of what no other class can do, or equivalent)
The response weighs the 10-week launch date against the effort of a custom build
The response keeps matching the marketing site branding as a requirement to test on other classes
The response keeps integration with the customer portal login as a requirement to test on other classes
The response includes generating the C++ API reference from Doxygen or the source as a requirement
The response includes a named build owner requirement with monthly hours
The response recommends a hosted docs platform or a self-hosted generator class
The response presents the custom build's standing cost as a platform team for the life of the site, or equivalent
